summary: Adds simple extensions to the Link Management Protocol so neighboring label-switching routers can confirm the status of data channels. This helps find stranded resources and triggers notifications when something does not match. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Neighbors check that each cable is really in use as both think, and shout if they disagree.

questions: how to find stranded resources in gmpls
what is lmp data channel status confirmation
what are stranded resources in gmpls
subtitle: Three new LMP messages let neighboring optical switches compare notes on which data channels are in use, so stranded resources can be found.

tldr.problem: The two ends of a data channel can disagree about whether it is in use. Such stranded resources are wasted, can make LSP setup fail, and are hard to find by auditing.
tldr.mechanism: Neighbors exchange ConfirmDataChannelStatus, Ack and Nack messages over the LMP control channel, compare channel statuses and report any mismatch to the management plane.
tldr.outcome: The control plane gets a tool to detect and isolate mismatches, meant to run periodically or on demand. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 6898.

today: RFC 5818 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2010. It has been updated by RFC 6898 and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Data Channel Mismatch Problem
sections.content:
In a GMPLS network, Label Switching Routers (LSRs) are joined by Traffic Engineering (TE) links, and each TE link is built from data channels. A data channel is a resource label in a non-packet technology, such as a timeslot or a lambda. A mismatch exists when the LSR at one end believes the channel is assigned to carry data and the LSR at the other end does not.

Routing protocols cannot reliably show this. Advertised bandwidth may reveal some mismatches on bidirectional links, but not with unidirectional services or multiple mismatches, and nothing tells which channel is at fault. A mismatch makes any new LSP that uses the channel fail, and it can cause misconnections in the data plane when LSPs are set up by the management plane.

Mismatched channels are often called stranded resources. They carry no LSP but cannot be assigned because they look in use. Auditing for them from the management plane is rarely done, because coordinating different Element Management Systems is hard and releasing an in-use resource by accident is risky. The RFC adds a control plane mechanism to detect and report them, built on LMP because LMP is already used to verify data plane connectivity.
sections.eli5: Imagine a seesaw seat that one kid thinks is taken and the other thinks is free. Nobody can use it properly, and nobody notices.

sections.title: How Mismatches Happen
sections.content:
The RFC gives three scenarios. In each, the channel is wasted and later LSP setup may fail.

  • Manual configuration: an operator sets a cross-connect at only one end of a TE link using an EMS. One end looks allocated while the other still looks free.
  • LSP deletion: if deletion is aborted midway, for example because a node resets abnormally, some nodes drop their cross-connects while another keeps its own. In the RFC's example, node B resets while an LSP across A, B and C is being deleted, so both links are left mismatched.
  • Failed resources: a termination point may look failed at one end and fine at the other, which can break bidirectional LSP setup.

RSVP soft state and RSVP-TE restart procedures help keep state consistent, but mismatches may arise after a restart and not be cleared up by it. The RFC says the need comes from operational concerns rather than a gap in GMPLS, since GMPLS networks co-exist with legacy networks and procedures. It expects human mistakes to be the major source, and it does not try to deal with broken implementations.
sections.eli5: Mismatches happen when someone flips a switch on only one side, when a cleanup stops halfway, or when one side thinks a part is broken and the other does not.

sections.title: The New LMP Messages
sections.content:
Three new messages run on the LMP control channel, carried in UDP as RFC 4204 defines. They are sent periodically or on an event such as an operator command, a configurable timer or an LSP setup rejected because of an unavailable resource.

  • ConfirmDataChannelStatus tells the remote end the status of the local end of one or more data channels and asks for the remote status. It contains a Common Header, LOCAL_LINK_ID, MESSAGE_ID and one or more DATA_LINK objects.
  • ConfirmDataChannelStatusAck returns the requested statuses, whether or not they match. Its MESSAGE_ID_ACK MUST come from the message being acknowledged.
  • ConfirmDataChannelStatusNack carries an ERROR_CODE. Code 0x01 means the procedure is not supported and 0x02 means unwilling to confirm. After an unwilling Nack, the sender MAY retry after a configured time, with 10 minutes suggested as a default.

A new Data Channel Status subobject goes inside the DATA_LINK object. It holds a 16-bit status and a Data Channel ID encoded as a label value. Status 0x0000 means available or free and 0x0001 means unavailable or in use. For SONET/SDH the ID identifies each timeslot and uses the encoding of RFC 4606.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of notes. One asks "is this cable in use on your side?", one answers, and one says "I can't do that."

sections.title: How the Confirmation Works
sections.content:
Starting a confirmation is a local policy decision. The SENDER builds a ConfirmDataChannelStatus message with one or more DATA_LINK objects, each with Data Channel Status subobjects that name the channel and report its status at the sender.

The RECEIVER MUST extract the statuses and SHOULD compare them with its own. A mismatch SHOULD be reported to the management plane, whose procedures are outside this document. The receiver also SHOULD send an Ack carrying its local statuses. If it cannot support or begin the procedure it MUST send a Nack. On receiving the Ack, the SENDER MUST compare the remote and local statuses and SHOULD report any mismatch.

The message SHOULD use LMP reliable transmission. If no Ack or Nack arrives after the retry limit, the sender SHOULD stop the procedure and SHOULD raise an alert to the management plane. A message that is not recognized is ignored and gets no reply. An out-of-order message, one whose MESSAGE_ID is lower than the largest previously received for that TE link, SHOULD be treated as such.

RSVP restart or soft-state timeout may fix a mismatch by itself. The procedures are meant for periodic or on-demand use, and it is NOT RECOMMENDED to use them for continuous on-line monitoring.
sections.eli5: One side lists its cables and says which are busy. The other side checks against its own list and answers. If the lists disagree, someone tells the people in charge.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility
sections.content:
Older nodes that only know the message types of RFC 4204 cannot recognize the three new messages. How LMP nodes should treat an unknown message is not specified in RFC 4204 and is left to a separate document.

Because legacy behavior must be assumed to be unknown, the RFC assumes that a deployment using this function consists completely of nodes that support the extensions. It notes that LMP may later be extended so that function support can be detected, which could make mixed deployments possible.
sections.eli5: Old devices do not understand the new notes, so every device in the group must know the new language first.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The LMP security measures from RFC 4204 apply to the new messages. The procedures do not change network state by themselves, so they are not a security risk on their own. If messages were intercepted or spoofed, however, bogus alerts could reach the management plane, so using the LMP security measures is RECOMMENDED. The RFC adds that running the procedures may help verify that data channels have not been illicitly modified.
sections.eli5: The notes only ask questions, so they cannot break anything. But a fake note could cause a false alarm, so they should be locked with LMP's protection.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA made three allocations in the LMP registries. In the LMP Message Type subregistry, value 32 is ConfirmDataChannelStatus, 33 is ConfirmDataChannelStatusAck and 34 is ConfirmDataChannelStatusNack. In the DATA_LINK Sub-object registry, value 9 is Data Channel Status. For the ERROR_CODE object, C-Type 4 is allocated to ConfirmDataChannelStatusNack.
sections.eli5: The number registry gave each new note and each new label its own number so nobody mixes them up.

messages.label: ConfirmDataChannelStatusAck
messages.note: Returns receiver-side statuses, match or not.

messages.label: ConfirmDataChannelStatusNack
messages.note: Instead of the Ack when unsupported or unwilling.
